decisions.rationale: Reproduced on a git archive of a942501c with the private completed work and one added probe rule each: a forwards-filled keyframes animation that holds the day tag at a different width, an infinite keyframes animation that scales both tags, and a forwards-filled animation that holds the overnight tag's padding at a different size each pass all 12 tests, while the same page read in the pinned Chromium after 300ms without the test's neutralisation draws the tags at the wrong size or padding. At the loop-3 lab state 3d48ec9a the width-holding and scaling variants fail task 11, so the loop-4 change that sets animation to none with importance while measuring opened this false pass. The test therefore measures a page the learner never sees, which makes the task 11 Outcome ('exactly 200px wide on screen') and README 'What the tests check' ('It rejects scaling ... a tag') false for an animated tag, and the solved-run record has no animation variant. Medium is the right grade: a wrong page passes, but only after a deliberate keyframes rule, and the calculated width is still required. The transition half of the loop-4 change is sound and should stay. Smallest correct fix: keep transitions neutralised, stop forcing animation to none, and instead call finish() on every finite animation of the checklist and both tags before measuring, leaving infinite animations to be measured as drawn, then update the lab.json notes phrase and add animation-held variants to the solved-run matrix. I prototyped exactly that two-line change in a separate archive of a942501c: the three wrong variants above each fail task 11 only (the infinite scale is caught by the existing unscaled check), while the completed work, a 2s no-fill entrance animation, an infinite colour animation and 5s all-property transitions on the checklist and tags each pass all 12. The critic's extra step of inspecting infinite animations' keyframes for a clearer message is optional polish, not required for correctness.

Reproduced on a git archive of a942501c and of 3d48ec9a: the private completed work plus a zoom on the gear checklist itself passes all 12 tests at both commits, while the unmodified page draws both tags clearly wider than the stated width. The pinned() map resets transform, scale, rotate, translate and zoom on the checklist with inline importance, so the rendered-width check only sees scaling from ancestors above it. This predates loop 4 and is an unlikely edit that still requires the calculated width, so low is correct, but it is a real false pass against the Outcome's 'on screen' requirement. Smallest correct fix: before pinning, read the checklist's own computed transform, scale, rotate, translate and zoom (after animations are settled as in cl4-sme-001) and fail with a checklist-specific message when any is not at its identity value.

Reproduced on a git archive of a942501c with the private completed work: floated tags and absolutely positioned tags fail only task 11 on the fill control, and because the browser blockifies those boxes the message prints 'its display is block' inside a clause that says the tag is not an ordinary block, which reads as self-contradictory; inline-block tags print their real display correctly. The pass or fail outcome is right and float and positioning are still named, so this is low message polish, and it is the same defect as part 1 of cl4-edu-001. Smallest correct fix: build the cause from the reason actually detected, printing the display only when it is an inline or table value and otherwise saying the tag is floated or absolutely positioned.

Both parts reproduced on a git archive of a942501c with the private completed work. Part 1 is the blockified 'its display is block' wording for floated and absolutely positioned tags, the same defect as cl4-sme-003. Part 2: tags given a display of contents fail only task 11 on the fill control, and the message blames something around the tag, because ownLayout does not recognise that display value; README Troubleshooting says 'the message names the cause', which is false for this case. A display of contents on a padded, bordered tag is an implausible edit and the outcome is still a correct failure, so low is the right grade. Smallest correct fix: together with the cl4-sme-003 change, also treat a display of contents as a tag-side cause and name it, which makes the README sentence true for this case without editing it; I did not test other no-box cases.
